subject: Post-call qualification: deployment preference and cost scenarios for Nimbus Analytics
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@nimbus.ai>, Rajesh Singh <rajesh@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: deployment preferences + next steps

Hi Alice / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our discovery and a few clarifying questions so we can build the right pricing scenarios: 

Key points I captured:
- Primary workload: user-facing analytics queries (multi-turn natural language queries + summarization).
- Data: mix of user PII and internal business metrics; must be isolated and have strict audit logs.
- Expected steady throughput: ~50 QPS inference today; peak bursts up to ~120 QPS during business hours.
- Latency target: 95th ~120ms, 99th <200ms (important for interactive UI).
- Timeline: procurement decision by end of Q4; pilot in Nov.

Clarifying questions so we can model costs appropriately: 
1) Deployment preference: do you lean toward Private VPC/on-prem (regulatory reasons) or are you open to Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Hosted API for an initial pilot?
2) If Dedicated or Private, do you expect to sign a 12-month committed capacity, or prefer a shorter reserved window?
3) Any specific compliance constraints (SOC2 Type II in-scope systems, data residency, or contractual DPA clauses) beyond what we discussed?
4) Budget ballpark for first 12 months (including infra + support)? This helps us recommend the right capacity breakpoints.

I attached a short attachment stub with the items we mentioned (security checklist you referenced).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm deployment preference + budget range.
- I produce three rough cost scenarios (Hosted per-token, Dedicated reserved commits, Private VPC on-prem OPEX+CAPEX) and share an internal TCO one-pager.
- Align on procurement owners so we can add procurement/legal to the thread if needed.

Regards,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few answers inline: 

1) Deployment preference: Our legal and security teams prefer Private VPC or on-prem for production because we process regulated customer data. That said, we're open to starting with Hosted API for a 6-8 week pilot if the data can be pseudonymized and we have a clear path to move to Private/Dedicated. We want to avoid a complete forklift.

2) Commitment: If Dedicated or Private makes sense technically, we're prepared to discuss a 12-month reserved commit for predictable unit economics. For Private on-prem we will evaluate capex vs managed offering costs.

3) Compliance: SOC 2 is required; we also need support for customer-driven data retention rules and an audit log accessible to our auditors. Data residency: US-only for the initial deployment.

4) Budget: Ballpark $300k–$400k ARR for the first 12 months (inclusive of infra, support, and a modest services ramp). We can expand if latency/SLOs require significantly more capacity.

Procurement / Legal: looping in Rajesh (cc) — he'll coordinate vendor paperwork and define procurement milestones.

Attaching: Nimbus internal security summary (see attached).

Best,
Alice Park

Karthik / Marissa —

Reviewed Alice's note and Karthik's workbook. High-level guidance and numbers (very rough, to be turned into a customer-facing PDF):

Scenario A — Hosted pilot
- Pilot (6 weeks) with Hosted API using the r-large family model: ~8M tokens/month for pilot = ~$6,400/month in consumption (per-token estimate 0.0008 per token blended) + monitoring/support credits. 12-month extrapolation (if they stayed hosted) ~ $76k (but does not include enterprise support or private routing).

Scenario B — Dedicated (Reserved commit)
- Recommended starting pool: 2xA100 equivalent for steady 50 QPS with efficient batching, headroom for bursts via autoscale to 4xA100-equivalents.
- 12-month reserved commit (monthly equivalent): ~$18k–$22k/month (committed), plus burst/overage at unit-based rate. Annual committed total approx $216k–$264k. Includes SLA and dedicated tenancy.

Scenario C — Private VPC / On-prem
- Managed Private (our hosted Private VPC): setup fee $30k, monthly managed service $12k/month + infra usage (expected $8k–$12k/month) => first-year total ~$210k–$260k (includes managed services).
- On-prem (customer buys hardware): rough CAPEX for two GPU nodes + networking & rack ~$450k–$600k (one-time) plus software license/annual support ~$50k/year. Ops: estimate 6–8 weeks for onboarding and an additional 2–3 FTE-weeks of integration consultancy.

Recommendation:
- Given their desire to pilot quickly and strict compliance needs, propose a hybrid: Hosted pilot (6–8 weeks) with clear export paths and data pseudonymization, then cutover to Dedicated or Private VPC under a 12-month reserved commit. This minimizes time-to-value while preserving a route to compliance.

Next steps:
1) I'll convert these bullets into a one-page TCO + appendix with assumptions and unit rates.
2) Karthik: propose a 30-min pilot scoping call with Alice/Rajesh this week to lock the pilot model and SLO matrix.
3) Marissa: can you validate the GPU sizing assumptions and draft the Dedicated configuration options?

I'll attach a short summary PDF once formatted.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
